JOB SUMMARY:
The Vessel Master will carry out duties as directed by the General Manager or Farm Managers.

Approximate start date: December 2026 & January 2027, AFE will be taking successful candidates throughout 2026/27 for these positions. Employment may be up to 4 years.

Renumeration:
The position is a Award Hourly Rate or Salary, paid on a fortnightly basis.
Vessel work completed inshore and onshore will be calculated at the nominated Farm rate.
(https://www.fairwork.gov.au/employment-conditions/awards/awards-summary/ma000114-summary)(https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000114.html)
An additional contract is put in place to cover the periods offshore for Tow & Support (if applicable).

Operations:
Periods at sea are varied and weather dependent. Hours of operation are determined by the daily operational needs. Farm vessels can be required to conduct operations year round from land based sites out to the farming site. The season begins in December finishing with the annual harvest period throughout June, July & August.
January – July Operations are 7 days per week; you can work up to 6 days in a week. Up to 12 hours per day.
August to December Operations are 5 days per week Monday to Friday, you will work up to 5 days in a week, 8 hours per day.

Vessel Master Duties:
The Employee will be required to perform certain duties whilst Master of the Vessel. Although this list is not exhaustive, it is a generalised overview of duties.
• Ensure crew work in such a way, to minimize risks to their health, safety, and others.
• Being involved in and overseeing the induction and ongoing training of crew and ensure safe work practices are continually developed and maintained. Ensure that all training is recorded on communication forms and passed on to the Farm Manager.
• Ensuring that only employees and approved maintenance contractors come onboard or attend any work sites.
• Documenting bait received, fed out, uneaten feed and daily fish behaviour.
• Report daily to the Farm Manager.
• Directing and training crew on feeding in accordance with daily feed plans and correct feeding techniques.
• Working the vessel within the regulations and relevant fisheries management rules. Ensuring that you are familiar with restricted areas regarding other farming operations, fisheries licensing conditions, national parks and within the bounds of safe and good seamanship.
• Keeping the vessel clean, tidy, and safe with safety and spare equipment accessible and organized.
• Ensuring the engine room is operating properly. The skipper is ultimately responsible for the whole vessel.
• Routinely checking all is in order and secure and dry in the chain locker, void spaces, bilge, steering compartment etc. (This is just basic seamanship and neglecting this responsibility is not acceptable).
• Routinely checking lifting gear is in a safe state (blocks, wire, ropes, shackles, hoses).
• Ensuring vessel is berthed properly and manned sufficiently, not leaving inexperienced deckhands to be responsible for securing the vessel.
• Ensuring all necessary gear, oils, jobs etc. are ordered and performed in a timely manner
• Carry out farm maintenance and repairs as required by The Farm Manager.
• Assisting in transfer of tuna to farms

• Ensuring own qualifications are kept up to date.
